summary: Patrick Pranke works in Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2004 under doctoral supervisors Luis Oscar Gómez and Victor B. Lieberman.
Patrick R. Uhlmann is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a PhD candidate at the University of California, Los Angeles, under Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Pattaratorn Chirapravati works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Cornell University (~1988–1994) and held posts at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (1997–2002), Sonoma State University (1997–2002), and California State University, Sacramento (2002–2016).
Paul B. Courtright is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro (~1974–1989) and Emory University (~1989–2018).

Paul B. Donnelly works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Geshe Lhundub Sopa (1989–1997) and also studied under several traditional teachers, later holding a post at Northern Arizona University (~1997).

Paul Bernard was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne (concluding in 1983) and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1980–1997).
Paul Carus was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Hermann Grassmann. He held a long-standing post at the Open Court Publishing Company (~1887–1919).

Paul Copp specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1996–1999) and Princeton University (~1999–2005, PhD under Stephen F. Teiser), later holding posts at Western Michigan University, Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, and University of Chicago.
Paul Crowe is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Calgary (~1995–1999) under Leslie S. Kawamura and became a professor at Simon Fraser University in ~2004.

Paul David Numrich specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Michigan in 1992 and held posts at Loyola University Chicago and the Theological Consortium of Greater Columbus.

Paul Demiéville was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot, later serving as Director of Buddhist Studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1945–1964) and Chair at Collège de France (1946–1964).

Paul Deussen was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1864–1866) under Christian Lassen and at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1867–1869), later serving as a professor at the University of Kiel (~1889–1919).
Paul Dundas was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and later served there as a professor from ~1976 to 2017.

Paul Fredericq was an historian who studied at Ghent University (~1866–1871) and the University of Liège (~1871–1875). He held faculty posts at the University of Liège (~1879–1883) and Ghent University (~1883–1919).
Paul Fuller is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied under Paul Dundas and completed his PhD at the University of Bristol (~2000–2004) under doctoral supervisor Rupert Gethin.

Paul G. Hackett specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having studied at Columbia University (-2002). He has held positions as a lecturer at Columbia University and as a curator and bibliographer at the University of Virginia.

Paul Groner specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1973) and earned his PhD from Yale University (~1971–1979), subsequently serving as a professor at the University of Virginia (~1980–2018).

Paul Hacker was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Berlin, Frankfurt, Heidelberg, and Bonn (habilitation 1949). He held posts at the University of Münster (1950–1978), Mithila Research Institute (1954–1955), and the Indology chair at the University of Bonn (1955–1963).

Paul Harrison specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He earned degrees from the University of Auckland and the Australian National University (PhD ~1974–1980), subsequently holding faculty posts at Auckland, the University of Canterbury (1983–2002), and Stanford University (2001–2010).

Paul J. Griffiths works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Oxford and Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1980–1983 under Minoru Kiyota), he held appointments at Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago, Notre Dame, University of Illinois Chicago, and Duke University.
